cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's accounting machine build the October financial statements for HANGS Construction, and compare them with the budget.
First, it reads the adjusted trial balance: every account's balance, after the month-end corrections.
The balance sheet lists what the company owns and owes. The income statement shows October's profit: about $14,600.
Then, where the cash came from and went.
Budget versus actual compares each line with the plan. Seven lines are off by more than $5,000 and 10 percent, and one has no explanation yet.
A covenant is a limit the lender sets. All three are met, but one has just 4.5 percent of room.
Last, it writes the workpapers and a draft package for the controller, the head of accounting, unsigned and unsent.

All done. October's profit is about $14,600 against a $134,660 budget, mostly because a sale moved to November. The year so far shows about $167,000. Four items need a person, including an unexplained variance and thin room on one covenant. Nothing is posted or sent until the controller releases it.
